questions.q: Equal masses of $\text{H}_{2}$, $\text{O}_{2}$ and methane have been taken in a container of volume V at temperature 27°C in identical conditions. The ratio of the volumes of gases $\text{H}_{2}$ : $\text{O}_{2}$ : $\text{CH}_{4}$ would be :
questions.s: At the same temperature and pressure, volume is proportional to moles. For equal mass m, moles are m/2 : m/32 : m/16. Multiplying by 32/m gives 16 : 1 : 2.

questions.q: When 22.4 litres of $\text{H}_{2}$(g) is mixed with 11.2 litres of $\text{Cl}_{2}$(g), each at S.T.P., the moles of HCl (g) formed is equal to :-
questions.s: 22.4 L of $\text{H}_{2}$ is 1 mol and 11.2 L of $\text{Cl}_{2}$ is 0.5 mol. $\text{H}_{2}$ + $\text{Cl}_{2}$ → 2HCl, so chlorine runs out first. 0.5 mol of $\text{Cl}_{2}$ gives 1 mol of HCl.

questions.q:
1.0 g of magnesium is burnt with 0.56 g $\text{O}_{2}$ in a closed vessel. Which reactant is left in excess and how much?
(At. wt. Mg = 24 ; O = 16)
questions.s: 2Mg + $\text{O}_{2}$ → 2MgO. Oxygen = 0.56/32 = 0.0175 mol needs 0.035 mol Mg = 0.84 g. Mg left = 1.0 − 0.84 = 0.16 g.

questions.q: A mixture of gases contains $\text{H}_{2}$ and $\text{O}_{2}$ gases in the ratio of 1 : 4 (w/w). What is the molar ratio of the two gases in the mixture ?
questions.s: Moles = mass/molar mass. $\text{H}_{2}$: 1/2 = 0.5 and $\text{O}_{2}$: 4/32 = 0.125. The ratio is 0.5 : 0.125 = 4 : 1.

questions.q: The number of water molecules is maximum in :-
questions.s: 18 moles of water has 18 × $6.02\times10^{23}$ molecules. 18 g is only 1 mole, 1.8 g is 0.1 mole and 18 molecules is almost nothing. So 18 moles has the most.

questions.q: If avogadro number $N_A$, is changed from $6.022\times10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1}$ to $6.022\times10^{20}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, this would change :
o: the ratio of chemical species to each other in a balanced equation
the ratio of elements to each other in a compound
the definition of mass in units of grams
the mass of one mole of carbon
questions.s: One mole is $N_A$ particles. If $N_A$ becomes smaller, one mole holds fewer atoms, so one mole of carbon would weigh less than 12 g. Ratios in equations and compounds depend only on relative numbers, so they stay the same.

questions.q:
20.0 g of a magnesium carbonate sample decomposes on heating to give carbon dioxide and 8.0g magnesium oxide. What will be the percentage purity of magnesium carbonate in the sample?
(At. Wt. : Mg = 24)
questions.s: $\text{MgCO}_{3}$ → MgO + $\text{CO}_{2}$. 8.0 g of MgO = 8/40 = 0.2 mol, so 0.2 mol of $\text{MgCO}_{3}$ reacted = 0.2 × 84 = 16.8 g. Purity = 16.8/20 × 100 = 84%.

questions.q: What is the mole fraction of the solute in a 1.00 m aqueous solution?
questions.s: 1.00 m means 1 mol of solute in 1000 g of water. Moles of water = 1000/18 = 55.5. Mole fraction of solute = 1/(1 + 55.5) = 0.0177.

questions.q: Suppose the elements X and Y combine to form two compounds $\text{XY}_{2}$ and $\text{X}_{3}\text{Y}_{2}$. When 0.1 mole of $\text{XY}_{2}$ weighs 10 g and 0.05 mole of $\text{X}_{3}\text{Y}_{2}$ weighs 9 g, the atomic weights of X and Y are
questions.s: Molar masses: $\text{XY}_{2}$ = 10/0.1 = 100 and $\text{X}_{3}\text{Y}_{2}$ = 9/0.05 = 180. So X + 2Y = 100 and 3X + 2Y = 180. Subtracting gives 2X = 80, so X = 40 and Y = 30.

questions.q:
A mixture of 2.3 g formic acid and 4.5 g oxalic acid is treated with conc. $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$. The evolved gaseous mixture is passed through KOH pellets. Weight (in g) of the remaining product at STP will be
(i) HCOOH → CO + $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ (conc. $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$; $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ absorbed by $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$)
(ii) $\text{H}_{2}\text{C}_{2}\text{O}_{4}$ → CO + $\text{CO}_{2}$ + $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ (conc. $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$; $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ absorbed by $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$)
(iii) $\text{CO}_{2}$ is absorbed by KOH
questions.s: Formic acid 2.3 g = 0.05 mol gives 0.05 mol CO. Oxalic acid 4.5 g = 0.05 mol gives 0.05 mol CO and 0.05 mol $\text{CO}_{2}$. KOH absorbs $\text{CO}_{2}$, so 0.1 mol CO is left = 0.1 × 28 = 2.8 g.

questions.q: In which case the number of molecules of water is maximum?
o: 0.00224 L of water vapours at 1 atm and 273 K
questions.s: 18 mL of water weighs 18 g (density 1 g/mL), which is 1 mol. The others are 0.01 mol, 0.0001 mol and 0.001 mol. So 18 mL has the most molecules.

questions.q: The number of moles of hydrogen molecules required to produce 20 moles of ammonia through Haber's process is :-
questions.s: $\text{N}_{2}$ + 3$\text{H}_{2}$ → 2$\text{NH}_{3}$. 3 mol of $\text{H}_{2}$ give 2 mol of $\text{NH}_{3}$. So 20 mol of $\text{NH}_{3}$ needs 20 × 3/2 = 30 mol of $\text{H}_{2}$.

questions.q:
The volume occupied by 1.8 g of water vapour at 374 °C and 1 bar pressure will be :-
[Use R = 0.083 bar L $K^{-1}$$mol^{-1}$]
Which one of the following has maximum number of atoms?
questions.s: For the same mass, the lightest atoms give the most atoms. Moles of atoms: Li = 1/7, Mg = 1/24, Ag = 1/108, and $\text{O}_{2}$ = 1/16 (as atoms). So lithium has the most.

questions.q: One mole of carbon atom weighs 12 g, the number of atoms in it is equal to, (Mass of carbon – 12 is $1.9926\times10^{-23}$ g)
questions.s: Number of atoms = 12 g / mass of one atom = 12/$1.9926\times10^{-23}$ = $6.022\times10^{23}$. This count is Avogadro's number.

questions.q: An organic comopound contains 78% (by wt.) carbon and remaining percentage of hydrogen. The right option for the empirical formula of this compound is [Atomic wt. of C is 12, H is 1]
questions.s: C = 78/12 = 6.5 and H = 22/1 = 22. The ratio C : H is about 1 : 3.4. The numbers are not exact, but $\text{CH}_{3}$ is the closest choice.

questions.q: An organic compound on analysis gave C = 54.5%, H = 9.1% by mass. Its empirical formula is
questions.s: O = 100 − 54.5 − 9.1 = 36.4%. Moles: C = 4.54, H = 9.1, O = 2.275. Dividing by 2.275 gives 2 : 4 : 1, so the formula is $\text{C}_{2}\text{H}_{4}\text{O}$.

questions.q: If 1 mL of water contains 20 drops then number of molecules in a drop of water is
questions.s: One drop = 1/20 mL = 0.05 mL, which is 0.05 g of water. Moles = 0.05/18 = $2.78\times10^{-3}$. Molecules = $2.78\times10^{-3}\times6.023\times10^{23} = 1.673\times10^{21}$.

questions.q: A sample of phosphorous trichloride ($\text{PCl}_{3}$) contains 1.4 moles of the substance. How many atoms are there in the sample?
questions.s: Each $\text{PCl}_{3}$ molecule has 4 atoms (1 P and 3 Cl). So 1.4 mol has 1.4 × 4 = 5.6 mol of atoms. Atoms = 5.6 × $6.022\times10^{23}$ = $3.372\times10^{24}$.

questions.q: In one molal solution that contains 0.5 mole of a solute, there is
questions.s: Molality is moles of solute per kg of solvent. A 1 molal solution with 0.5 mol of solute needs 0.5 kg = 500 g of solvent.

questions.q:
What mass of 95% pure $\text{CaCO}_{3}$ will be required to neutralise 50 mL of 0.5 M HCl solution according to the following reaction ?
$\text{CaCO}_{3}$(s) + 2HCl(aq) → $\text{CaCl}_{2}$(aq) + $\text{CO}_{2}$(g) + 2$\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$(l)
[Calculate upto second place of decimal point]

Match List-I with List-II :
(Given : Molar volume of a gas at STP=22.4 L)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.s: (a) 4.48 L of $\text{O}_{2}$ is 0.2 mol, which is 6.4 g. (b) $12.022\times10^{22}$ molecules of water is 0.2 mol. (c) 96 g of $\text{O}_{2}$ is 3 mol, which is 67.2 L. (d) 88 g of $\text{CO}_{2}$ is 2 mol, which is $12.044\times10^{23}$ molecules.

questions.q: The density of the solution is 2.15 g $mL^{-1}$, then mass of 2.5 mL solution in correct significant figures is
questions.s: Mass = 2.15 × 2.5 = 5.375 g. In multiplication, the answer keeps as many significant figures as the least precise number. 2.5 has 2, so the answer is 5.4 g.

questions.q:
The right option for the mass of $\text{CO}_{2}$ produced by heating 20 g of 20% pure limestone is
(Atomic mass of Ca = 40)
[$\text{CaCO}_{3}$ → $\text{CaO}$ + $\text{CO}_{2}$ (1200 K)]
questions.s: Pure $\text{CaCO}_{3}$ = 20% of 20 g = 4 g = 0.04 mol (molar mass 100). $\text{CaCO}_{3}$ → CaO + $\text{CO}_{2}$, so $\text{CO}_{2}$ = 0.04 mol × 44 = 1.76 g.
